title: Nun and samech (Berakhot 4b)
hookLine: nun is missing from Ashrei, but the next verse says God upholds all who fall

lines: A PSALM BUILT LETTER BY LETTER.
cards: Psalm one hundred forty-five is built like a ladder. Each verse begins with the next letter of the alef-bet: alef, then bet, then gimel, climbing in order.

Jews know it as Ashrei, from the words said just before it in the prayer book, and it comes up again and again in the daily services. Say it slowly, and somewhere past the middle a rung is gone. After mem comes samech.
There's no verse for nun. A missing letter in a prayer said that often is the kind of thing the rabbis could not leave alone.

teach.h: WHY NO NUN? THE TALMUD ASKS.
teach.b: The Talmud asks it in tractate Berakhot: why is there no nun in Ashrei? Rabbi Yochanan answers: because a verse that begins with nun tells of Israel's fall.

teach.h: AMOS: FALLEN, AND WILL NOT RISE.
teach.b: He points to the prophet Amos, whose lament opens with the Hebrew word for fallen, nafelah: the maiden of Israel has fallen, and will not rise again.
A psalm of praise, the Talmud suggests, did not want to open a line with that word. Then another sage, Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak, carries it on: even so, David returned and held them up.

teach.h: THE NEXT VERSE: GOD UPHOLDS THE FALLEN.
teach.b: Look at the very next verse, the samech verse. In the old Jewish Publication Society translation: "The LORD upholdeth all that fall." In Hebrew it begins somech, supporting.
Somech Adonai l'chol hanoflim. The verse that lifts begins with samech, and its word for the fallen, noflim, comes from the same root Amos used.

teach.h: THE FALL IS HELD, NOT ERASED.
teach.b: So the fall isn't erased from the psalm. It's folded into the next line, already being held.

teach.h: THE LORD UPHOLDETH ALL THAT FALL.
teach.b: The empty space where nun should be is the moment of falling, and the line that catches it is right beneath.
Some readers hear a picture of how a fall should go in a community: nobody pretends it didn't happen, and nobody leaves the one who fell on the ground.
All of it inside a psalm said on an ordinary morning, before the day begins.

how: Psalm 145, called Ashrei, is part of the daily Jewish prayer services; its verses follow the alef-bet, and the Talmud in Berakhot 4b explains the missing nun verse by pointing to the samech verse that follows.

o: two letters: the one missing from Ashrei, and the one that lifts
the first and last letters of the Hebrew alphabet
two vowel marks that change how a Hebrew word sounds

games.q: nun and samech — tap the pairs.
p: a psalm built letter by letter

s: Ashrei has a verse for every letter of the alef-bet
it skips nun. after mem comes samech.
the Talmud links the missing nun to a verse about falling
Rabbi Yochanan points to Amos: the maiden of Israel has fallen.
the verse after the gap is about the fallen too
"the LORD upholdeth all that fall." it begins with samech.

games.q: you're compiling a psalm of praise, letter by letter. the only nun line you can think of is about falling and never rising. what do you do?
o: write the fall in anyway, right where it goes.
leave nun out, and let the next verse hold up the fallen.
games.why: the Talmud's answer: no nun verse, and the samech verse that follows says God upholds all who fall. the fall is held, not erased.

practice: Bring to mind someone who has stumbled lately: a friend who lost a job, a child who failed a test, a coworker who made a public mistake, maybe you.

Don't fix it yet; just notice where they are, on the ground or halfway up, and what it would look like to be the next line under them, a message, a coffee, a word that says the fall isn't the whole story.
If you pray, you can say the samech verse quietly.

wordCard.voice: Nun and samech. Nun, the missing rung in Ashrei, the letter of falling. Samech, the letter of the verse that holds up all who fall. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: supporting, holding up — the first word of the samech verse in Ashrei.

carryVoice: Your line: nun falls, samech lifts. The fall is held, not erased. See you tomorrow.
